precepts.text: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
precepts.point: Apollonius, pretending peace, forbare till the holy day of the Sabbath, and taking the Jews keeping holy day, commanded his men to arm themselves, and slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the Sabbath. But Judas Maccabeus with nine others withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, and fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.
precepts.why:
When a false rumour went out that Antiochus was dead, Jason took a thousand men and assaulted the city. “But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen.” He despised his own people.

“Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason.” You think you can be a traitor and be honored and respected? No. Nobody likes a traitor. Even in Rise of the Planet of the Apes, the whole movie is about black people, they spray painted the word donkey on the traitor apes. That is the brothers who were in here in 2018, and some of the brothers who just bugged out in LA. You cannot be trusted.

Christ spoke of what it is to harm his own: “But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.” It would be better for the betrayer to have a millstone hanged about his neck and be drowned.

Jason offended and slew those who belonged to the Lord, and he got his reward: shame, fleeing from city to city, and dying in a strange land.

precepts.text: Woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born. That is what the scripture says about the betrayer.
precepts.point: Apollonius, pretending peace, forbare till the holy day of the Sabbath, and taking the Jews keeping holy day, commanded his men to arm themselves, and slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the Sabbath. But Judas Maccabeus with nine others withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, and fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.
precepts.why:
Jason “received shame for the reward of his treason.” Christ spoke directly about the betrayer: “The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.” Put that with the millstone about the neck, and both mean the same thing for the traitor: go die.

See how all the evil Jason did came back on him. “In the end therefore he had an unhappy return, being accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt.”

“Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians”, that is Sparta, “thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred: And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.”

It had been good for that man if he had not been born. That is what the scripture says about the betrayer, whether it is Jason with Onias, Judas with Christ, or those who betray their brethren in this truth today.

precepts.text: Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that getting the day of his own nation would be a most unhappy day.
precepts.point: The traitor Jason slew his own countrymen to please the Greeks and died an exile.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Under the Greeks, “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and Syria and the Philistines joined in. Others helped the Greeks, and so did one of our own.

“But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.” Jason was an Israelite, and he hated his own people. We think our people love themselves; no. He treated us like enemies, because he wanted to please the Greeks. Don't be surprised when you see black men and black women do all they can to please the enemies of our people. They will be worse on you than white men.

Read on: “for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason”. He was a treasonous negro, and the Most High cannot stand a traitor. He was “fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen”, and “cast out into Egypt.” Imagine being banished, unable to come back to your own country because you were a traitor.

“Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land”, thinking to find succour among the Lacedemonians, where Sparta was. “And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.” What goes around comes around.

precepts.text: About the time of Antiochus' second voyage into Egypt, horsemen were seen running in the air, and on a false rumor of his death Jason assaulted the city and slew his own citizens without mercy.
precepts.point: He stirs up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south is stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army.

note.label: Daniel 11: The Kings of the North and the South

precepts.why:
“About the same time Antiochus prepared his second voyage into Egypt”. This is the king of the north stirring up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army: Antiochus going down into Egypt the second time.

About that time horsemen were seen running in the air, and on a false rumor of his death Jason assaulted the city and slew his own citizens without mercy.

precepts.point: Then he returns into his land with great riches, and his heart is against the holy covenant.

note.label: Daniel 11: The Kings of the North and the South

precepts.why: “So when Antiochus had carried out of the temple a thousand and eight hundred talents, he departed in all haste unto Antiochia, weening in his pride to make the land navigable, and the sea passable by foot: such was the haughtiness of his mind.” That is him returning into his land with great riches: a thousand and eight hundred talents stripped out of the temple, and governors left behind to vex the nation. His heart was against the holy covenant.

precepts.text: Pretending peace, they waited for the sabbath and slew great multitudes, but Judas Maccabeus withdrew into the wilderness and fed on herbs, lest they be partakers of the pollution.
precepts.point: Then he returns into his land with great riches, and his heart is against the holy covenant.

note.label: Daniel 11: The Kings of the North and the South

precepts.why:
His heart against the holy covenant shows in what was done on the sabbath. “Who coming to Jerusalem, and pretending peace, did forbear till the holy day of the sabbath, when taking the Jews keeping holy day, he commanded his men to arm themselves.” Pretending peace, they waited for the sabbath and slew great multitudes.

But Judas Maccabeus withdrew into the wilderness and fed on herbs, lest they be partakers of the pollution.

moments.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: Through all the city, for the space almost of forty days, there were seen horsemen running in the air, in cloth of gold, and armed with lances; and every man prayed that the apparition might turn to good.

When there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men and suddenly made an assault upon the city, and Menelaus fled into the castle. Now Menelaus is running from his one-time friend Jason, whose priesthood he took. But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, because he despised his own people.

Apollonius, pretending peace, forbare till the holy day of the Sabbath, and taking the Jews keeping holy day, commanded his men to arm themselves, and slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the Sabbath. But Judas Maccabeus with nine others withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, and fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.

Yet was he not content with this, but presumed to go into the most holy temple of all the world; Menelaus, that traitor to the laws, and to his own country, being his guide. An Israelite guided Esau on what to do. And besides Menelaus, the governors he left were worse than all the rest, bearing a heavy hand over the citizens, having a malicious mind against his countrymen the Jews. That is why to this day they look for those who will be harder on us than Esau, because they have something to prove.

Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason, and fled again into the country of the Ammonites. You think you can be a traitor and be honored and respected? Nobody likes a traitor; even in Rise of the Planet of the Apes, they spray painted the word donkey on the traitor apes. That is the brothers that left in 2018 and the brothers that just bugged out in LA. You cannot be trusted.

In the end therefore he had an unhappy return: accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt. Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retired to the Lacedemonians (that is Sparta); and he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers. All that evil he did came back on him.

When these doings came to the king's ear, he thought that Judea had revolted; he took the city by force of arms, and there were destroyed within the space of three whole days fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict, and no fewer sold than slain.

Jason, the wicked Israelite who slew his own citizens without mercy, fled again into the country of the Ammonites, and in the end was accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians. Why? Because by that time the Arabs controlled the land of the Ammonites.

Book read in class: The Antiquities of the Jews, by Flavius Josephus, book 13 chapter 15: Alexander Jannaeus "was forced to deliver back to the king of Arabia the land of Moab and Gilead which he had subdued," so that the Arabians would not join the war against him. The king of Arabia had the land of Moab as well. Context read in class: during the reign of the Hasmonean king Alexander Jannaeus (103 to 76 BC), the Nabataean kingdom, ruled by the king of Arabia, took those territories. The Nabataeans were Arabs; that is why foolish people online read that Edom was ruled by the Nabataeans and say Edom are the Arabs. The Nabataeans came later, during the time of the Maccabees.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

points: Reading from the research summary: the Moabites and Ammonites did not leave their ancestral lands in a single voluntary exodus; they vanished from the region between the sixth and first centuries BC through military devastation and forced exiles, from the time of Nebuchadnezzar to the time of the Greeks, in increments. But the claim that they simply blended into the newer Arab populations is not true; the AI summaries and search engines will mislead you on purpose so you never find out who Moab and Ammon are. Remember who controls them.
